stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether a new drug reduces anxiety. They recruited 150 adults diagnosed with generalized anxiety disorder and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition took the new drug every day for eight weeks. Participants in the other condition took a placebo pill that looked identical every day for eight weeks. The researchers then recorded each participant's score on a standard anxiety questionnaire after eight weeks.

Researchers collected data from 600 university students. For each one, they recorded conscientiousness score on a personality inventory and grade point average. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.35.

Researchers investigated whether cognitive-behavioral therapy reduces depression. They recruited 90 adults diagnosed with major depressive disorder and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition received twelve weekly sessions of cognitive-behavioral therapy. Participants in the other condition were placed on a waiting list for twelve weeks and were treated afterward. The researchers then recorded each participant's score on a standard depression questionnaire after twelve weeks.

Researchers investigated whether mindfulness meditation lowers stress. They recruited 84 office workers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition practiced mindfulness meditation for twenty minutes a day for eight weeks. Participants in the other condition listened to an audiobook for twenty minutes a day for eight weeks. The researchers then recorded the level of the stress hormone cortisol in a saliva sample from each participant.
Researchers collected data from 500 adults aged 20 to 80. For each one, they recorded age and score on a timed reasoning test. The correlation between the two measures was r = −0.55.

Researchers investigated whether the presence of other people slows the reporting of an emergency. They recruited 80 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition were filling in a form in a room with four other people when smoke began to enter the room. Participants in the other condition were filling in the form alone when smoke began to enter the room. The researchers then recorded the time in seconds before each participant left the room to report the smoke.

Researchers investigated whether an expected reward reduces children's later interest in drawing. They recruited 60 preschool children who enjoyed drawing and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition were promised a certificate for drawing and received it. Children in the other condition drew with no reward mentioned. The researchers then recorded the number of minutes that each child chose to spend drawing during free time one week later.

Researchers investigated whether spreading study sessions out improves long-term retention. They recruited 90 high school students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition studied a list of 40 words in six ten-minute sessions on six different days. Participants in the other condition studied the same list in a single sixty-minute session. The researchers then recorded the number of words out of 40 that each participant recalled on a test one month later. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.41.

rows.group: The group that studied in six short sessions
The group that studied in one long session

stimuli.text: Researchers collected data from 250 adults. For each one, they recorded resting heart rate and self-rated anxiety. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.38.

Researchers investigated whether the color of a drink affects the ability to identify its flavor. They recruited 70 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition tasted ten fruit drinks whose colors did not match their flavors. Participants in the other condition tasted the same ten drinks with matching colors. The researchers then recorded the number of flavors out of ten that each participant named correctly.

Researchers collected data from 300 families. For each one, they recorded the warmth of parenting, as rated by observers and the child's self-esteem score. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.48.

Researchers investigated whether praise increases hand raising in class. They recruited 50 second-grade students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition were praised by the teacher each time they raised a hand before speaking. Children in the other condition received no special response when they raised a hand. The researchers then recorded the number of times that each child raised a hand during one week.

Researchers collected data from 400 high school students. For each one, they recorded the average number of hours slept per night and grade point average. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.45.

Researchers investigated whether guided hints help children learn to solve puzzles. They recruited 64 five-year-old children and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition solved practice puzzles with hints from an adult that were gradually reduced. Children in the other condition solved the same practice puzzles alone. The researchers then recorded the number of new puzzles out of ten that each child later solved without help. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.01.

Read the summary of a hypothetical study, then answer parts A to F.

**Introduction.** Researchers investigated whether a phone conversation reduces what drivers notice. They hypothesized that phone use would affect attention to the road.

**Participants.** The sample was 64 licensed drivers, recruited from one city. All participants gave informed consent, were told they could withdraw at any time, and were debriefed afterward. The plan was approved by an institutional review board.

**Method.** The participants were randomly assigned to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition held a hands-free phone conversation while using a driving simulator. Participants in the other condition used the driving simulator without a phone. The researchers recorded the number of road signs out of 30 that each participant failed to notice.

**Results.** The group that talked on the phone: mean road signs missed (out of 30) = 11.4. The group that drove without a phone: mean road signs missed (out of 30) = 4.9. The difference was statistically significant (p = 0.01).

Use the three hypothetical sources to answer the question: **Which study methods lead to the best long-term learning?**

**Source A.** In an experiment, 90 students were randomly assigned to study 40 vocabulary words either in six ten-minute sessions on different days or in one sixty-minute session. One month later, the spaced group recalled a mean of 27 words and the single-session group a mean of 16 (p = 0.01).

**Source B.** In an experiment, 120 students read a passage and were randomly assigned either to take three practice quizzes or to reread the passage three times. On a test one week later, the quiz group scored a mean of 68 percent and the rereading group 49 percent (p = 0.01).

**Source C.** In a survey of 600 students, 71 percent said that rereading notes was their main study method, and most rated it as highly effective. Only 12 percent said that they regularly tested themselves.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the rare ability to recall almost every day of one's life in detail?

options.why: Maintenance rehearsal is the repeating of information over and over to keep it in short-term memory.
Correct. Highly superior autobiographical memory is the rare ability to recall almost every day of one's life in detail.
Autobiographical memory is the memory of the events of one's own life.
Elaborative rehearsal is the linking of new information to existing knowledge and meaning to store it in long-term memory.

questions.explanation: Highly superior autobiographical memory is the rare ability to recall almost every day of one's life in detail.

questions.stem: In the strange situation, a toddler approaches her mother, then freezes, then backs away with a dazed expression. Which attachment style is this?

options.why: Contact comfort is the comfort from physical touch that Harlow showed is more important to attachment than feeding.
Correct. Disorganized attachment is the insecure attachment style in which a child shows confused, contradictory behavior toward the caregiver.
Secure attachment is the attachment style in which a child uses the caregiver as a safe base, is upset when the caregiver leaves and is comforted on return.
Avoidant attachment is the insecure attachment style in which a child seems indifferent when the caregiver leaves and ignores the caregiver on return.

questions.explanation: Disorganized attachment is the insecure attachment style in which a child shows confused, contradictory behavior toward the caregiver.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes hoarding disorder?

options.text: The disorder in which a person has unwanted repeated thoughts and feels driven to perform repeated actions
options.why: That describes obsessive-compulsive disorder.

options.text: The disorder in which a person has flashbacks, nightmares, watchfulness and avoidance for more than a month after a terrifying event
options.why: That describes posttraumatic stress disorder.

options.text: The disorder in which a person cannot remember important personal information, usually after trauma and with no physical cause, sometimes with travel away from home (fugue)
options.why: That describes dissociative amnesia.

options.text: The disorder in which a person cannot throw away possessions, so that living spaces become cluttered
options.why: Correct. This is what hoarding disorder means.

questions.explanation: Hoarding disorder is the disorder in which a person cannot throw away possessions, so that living spaces become cluttered.

questions.stem: A second laboratory repeats a famous memory study with new participants to check the result. This is an example of which of the following?

options.why: Naturalistic observation is the research method of watching and recording behavior in its natural setting without interfering.
A correlational study is the research method that measures two variables to see how they are related, without manipulating either.
Correct. Replication is the repeating of a study with different participants to see whether the finding holds.
An experiment is the research method in which a researcher manipulates a variable and randomly assigns participants, which allows conclusions about cause and effect.

questions.explanation: Replication is the repeating of a study with different participants to see whether the finding holds.

questions.stem: During adolescence, the reproductive organs themselves mature. These organs are examples of which of the following?

options.why: Menopause is the natural end of menstruation and of the ability to reproduce, usually around age 50.
Puberty is the period of sexual maturation, when a person becomes able to reproduce.
Correct. Primary sex characteristics is the body structures, such as ovaries and testes, that make reproduction possible.
Secondary sex characteristics is the nonreproductive traits of sexual maturity, such as body hair and a deeper voice.

questions.explanation: Primary sex characteristics is the body structures, such as ovaries and testes, that make reproduction possible.

questions.stem: Which brain structure stores the well-practiced skill of riding a bicycle?

options.why: The medulla is the base of the brainstem, which controls heartbeat and breathing.
The pituitary gland is the master gland of the endocrine system, which is controlled by the hypothalamus.
The reticular activating system is the network of neurons in the brainstem that controls arousal and alertness.
Correct. The cerebellum is the structure at the back of the brainstem that coordinates balance, movement and procedural learning.

questions.explanation: The cerebellum is the structure at the back of the brainstem that coordinates balance, movement and procedural learning.

questions.stem: After his diagnosis becomes known, Raj is avoided by neighbors and passed over for jobs. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Dysfunction is the criterion for a disorder that the behavior interferes with daily life, such as work and relationships.
The ICD is the World Health Organization's international system for classifying all diseases, including mental disorders.
Distress is the criterion for a disorder that the behavior causes suffering to the person.
Correct. Stigma is the negative attitudes and discrimination directed at people who have a psychological disorder.

questions.explanation: Stigma is the negative attitudes and discrimination directed at people who have a psychological disorder.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the category of character strengths that includes creativity, curiosity and love of learning?

options.why: Justice is the category of character strengths that includes teamwork, fairness and leadership.
Correct. Wisdom is the category of character strengths that includes creativity, curiosity and love of learning.
Humanity is the category of character strengths that includes love, kindness and social intelligence.
Courage is the category of character strengths that includes bravery, honesty and perseverance.

questions.explanation: Wisdom is the category of character strengths that includes creativity, curiosity and love of learning.

questions.stem: Drugs that block dopamine receptors reduce the symptoms of schizophrenia. This finding supports which of the following?

options.why: A negative symptom is a symptom of schizophrenia that takes away a normal behavior, such as emotional expression or motivation.
A positive symptom is a symptom of schizophrenia that adds an inappropriate behavior or experience, such as hallucinations.
A chronic course is the slow, gradual development of schizophrenia, from which recovery is less likely.
Correct. The dopamine hypothesis is the idea that schizophrenia involves excessive activity of the neurotransmitter dopamine.

questions.explanation: The dopamine hypothesis is the idea that schizophrenia involves excessive activity of the neurotransmitter dopamine.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a personality inventory?

options.text: The belief in one's own ability to succeed at a particular task
options.why: That describes self-efficacy.

options.text: The statistical method that finds clusters of related test items, used to identify basic traits
options.why: That describes factor analysis.

options.text: The idea that a person's behavior, thoughts and environment all influence one another
options.why: That describes reciprocal determinism.

options.text: A questionnaire with many true-false or agree-disagree items that measures a range of traits
options.why: Correct. This is what a personality inventory means.

questions.explanation: A personality inventory is a questionnaire with many true-false or agree-disagree items that measures a range of traits.

questions.stem: A theorist argues that a gifted dancer and a gifted mathematician show different, separate kinds of intelligence. Which theory is this?

options.why: The intelligence quotient is originally, mental age divided by chronological age and multiplied by 100.
General intelligence is the single underlying mental ability that Spearman believed affects performance on all mental tasks.
Correct. Multiple intelligences is the theory that people have several independent kinds of intelligence, such as musical and interpersonal.
The Flynn effect is the steady rise in average intelligence test scores over the generations.

questions.explanation: Multiple intelligences is the theory that people have several independent kinds of intelligence, such as musical and interpersonal.

questions.stem: What is the independent variable in this study?

options.why: This was measured, not manipulated: it is the dependent variable.
Correct. The independent variable is the factor the researchers changed between the two conditions.

options.text: The number of participants in the study
options.why: This is the sample size, not a variable the researchers changed.
This is a procedure for forming the groups, not a variable.

questions.explanation: The independent variable is the factor the researchers changed between the two conditions.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the reinforcing of closer and closer approximations of a desired behavior?

options.why: The law of effect is Thorndike's principle that behaviors followed by good outcomes become more likely and those followed by bad outcomes become less likely.
Superstitious behavior is a behavior that is repeated because it happened by chance just before a reward.
Learned helplessness is the passive giving up that follows repeated experiences of being unable to avoid bad events.
Correct. Shaping is the reinforcing of closer and closer approximations of a desired behavior.

questions.explanation: Shaping is the reinforcing of closer and closer approximations of a desired behavior.

questions.stem: Rex looks for excitement through wild parties and reckless, uninhibited behavior. Which form of sensation seeking is this?

options.why: Correct. Disinhibition is the form of sensation seeking that involves a loss of self-restraint, as at wild parties.
Experience seeking is the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for new experiences through travel, art and unusual lifestyles.
Boredom susceptibility is the form of sensation seeking that involves a strong dislike of repetition and routine.
Thrill and adventure seeking is the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for risky physical activities.

questions.explanation: Disinhibition is the form of sensation seeking that involves a loss of self-restraint, as at wild parties.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as an explanation of behavior that points to outside circumstances?

options.why: Downward social comparison is the comparing of oneself with people who are doing worse.
An internal locus of control is the belief that a person controls their own outcomes through their own actions.
An external locus of control is the belief that outcomes are decided by luck, fate or other people.
Correct. A situational attribution is an explanation of behavior that points to outside circumstances.

questions.explanation: A situational attribution is an explanation of behavior that points to outside circumstances.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the bond of trust and cooperation between therapist and client?

options.why: Correct. The therapeutic alliance is the bond of trust and cooperation between therapist and client.
Deinstitutionalization is the movement, begun in the 1950s, of patients out of psychiatric hospitals and into community care.
Evidence-based practice is the choosing of treatments on the basis of research, clinical skill and the client's own values.
A meta-analysis is a statistical procedure that combines the results of many studies to reach an overall conclusion.

questions.explanation: The therapeutic alliance is the bond of trust and cooperation between therapist and client.

questions.stem: A child's parents and teachers meet regularly and work together. In ecological systems theory, this connection is part of which system?

options.why: The chronosystem is in ecological systems theory, the life stage and historical events that affect a child.
Correct. The mesosystem is in ecological systems theory, the relationships between the groups in a child's immediate surroundings.
The microsystem is in ecological systems theory, the groups that have direct contact with the child, such as family and school.
The exosystem is in ecological systems theory, the settings that affect a child indirectly, such as a parent's workplace.

questions.explanation: The mesosystem is in ecological systems theory, the relationships between the groups in a child's immediate surroundings.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the control group?

options.text: A procedure in which neither the participants nor the researchers who deal with them know who is in which condition
options.why: That describes a double-blind procedure.

options.text: A factor other than the independent variable that differs between groups and could explain the results
options.why: That describes a confounding variable.

options.text: The group in an experiment that does not receive the treatment and is used for comparison
options.why: Correct. This is what the control group means.

options.text: The conclusion that a result is unlikely to have occurred by chance, usually when p is below 0.05
options.why: That describes statistical significance.

questions.explanation: The control group is the group in an experiment that does not receive the treatment and is used for comparison.

questions.stem: What does the correlation show?

options.text: Higher values of the first measure tend to go with higher values of the second
options.why: Correct. A positive correlation means the two measures tend to move in the same direction.

options.text: The first measure causes the second
options.why: A correlation does not show cause and effect.

options.text: Higher values of the first measure tend to go with lower values of the second
options.why: That would be a negative correlation.
A correlation of zero would show no relationship.

questions.explanation: A positive correlation means the two measures tend to move in the same direction.

questions.stem: Mia's parents are loving but let her stay up as late as she likes and rarely enforce any rules. Which parenting style is this?

options.why: Authoritative parenting is the parenting style that sets firm rules but explains them, listens and is warm.
Temperament is a person's characteristic emotional reactivity and intensity, which appears early in life.
Correct. Permissive parenting is the parenting style that makes few demands and sets few limits.
Authoritarian parenting is the parenting style that sets strict rules and expects obedience, with little warmth or discussion.

questions.explanation: Permissive parenting is the parenting style that makes few demands and sets few limits.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the view that the different cultural groups in a society should be valued and should keep their identities?

options.why: Conformity is the adjusting of behavior or thinking to match a group standard.
The false consensus effect is the tendency to overestimate how many other people share our opinions and behaviors.
Correct. Multiculturalism is the view that the different cultural groups in a society should be valued and should keep their identities.
Obedience is the following of the direct commands of an authority figure.

questions.explanation: Multiculturalism is the view that the different cultural groups in a society should be valued and should keep their identities.

questions.stem: Which group served as the control group?

options.text: The group on the waiting list
options.why: Correct. The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.
Only the comparison group is the control group.

options.text: Neither group, because the study had no comparison condition
options.why: The second condition is the comparison.
This group received the treatment being tested: it is the experimental group.

questions.explanation: The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.

questions.stem: Which part of the working memory model decides what to attend to and coordinates the sound and visual stores?

options.why: The visuospatial sketchpad is the part of working memory that briefly holds images and spatial information.
Long-term potentiation is the strengthening of the connections between neurons after repeated activation, which is the biological basis of memory.
Correct. The central executive is the part of working memory that directs attention and coordinates the other parts.
The phonological loop is the part of working memory that briefly holds spoken and written words.

questions.explanation: The central executive is the part of working memory that directs attention and coordinates the other parts.

questions.stem: While chatting at a crowded party, Deshawn suddenly notices his own name spoken across the room. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Correct. The cocktail party effect is the ability to notice personally important information, such as your name, in an unattended conversation.
A perceptual set is a readiness to perceive something in a particular way because of expectations.
Change blindness is the failure to notice that something in the environment has changed.
Inattentional blindness is the failure to notice a visible object because attention is directed elsewhere.

questions.explanation: The cocktail party effect is the ability to notice personally important information, such as your name, in an unattended conversation.

questions.stem: A car crash damages a driver's spinal cord. Which part of the nervous system has been injured?

options.why: The sympathetic nervous system is the division of the autonomic nervous system that arouses the body for fight or flight.
The peripheral nervous system is the sensory and motor nerves that connect the brain and spinal cord to the rest of the body.
Correct. The central nervous system is the brain and spinal cord.
The autonomic nervous system is the division of the peripheral nervous system that controls glands and internal organs without conscious effort.

questions.explanation: The central nervous system is the brain and spinal cord.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the hormone released by the adrenal glands that raises heart rate and energy during stress?

options.why: Melatonin is the hormone released by the pineal gland that makes a person sleepy.
Ghrelin is the hormone released by an empty stomach that increases hunger.
Correct. Adrenaline is the hormone released by the adrenal glands that raises heart rate and energy during stress.
Leptin is the hormone released by fat cells that signals fullness and reduces hunger.

questions.explanation: Adrenaline is the hormone released by the adrenal glands that raises heart rate and energy during stress.

questions.stem: A researcher stores survey answers under code numbers so that no answer can be linked to a name. Which ethical requirement is this?

options.why: Deception is the misleading of participants about the true purpose of a study, allowed only when necessary and followed by debriefing.
An institutional review board is the committee that reviews research plans to make sure participants are treated ethically.
Correct. Confidentiality is the keeping private of participants' identities and data.
A confederate is a person who seems to be a participant but is secretly working for the researcher.

questions.explanation: Confidentiality is the keeping private of participants' identities and data.

questions.stem: After a coin lands heads five times in a row, Rita is sure the next toss must be tails. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: The availability heuristic is the judging of how likely something is by how easily examples come to mind.
Framing is the way the wording of an issue affects decisions and judgments.
The sunk-cost fallacy is the tendency to keep investing in something because of what has already been spent on it.
Correct. The gambler's fallacy is the mistaken belief that a random event is more likely because it has not happened recently.

questions.explanation: The gambler's fallacy is the mistaken belief that a random event is more likely because it has not happened recently.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the humanistic therapy in which the therapist provides acceptance and empathy so that the client can grow?

options.why: Free association is the psychodynamic technique in which the client says whatever comes to mind.
Active listening is the technique of echoing, restating and seeking clarification of what the client says.
Group therapy is the therapy in which several clients meet together with a therapist and benefit from each other's support.
Correct. Person-centered therapy is the humanistic therapy in which the therapist provides acceptance and empathy so that the client can grow.

questions.explanation: Person-centered therapy is the humanistic therapy in which the therapist provides acceptance and empathy so that the client can grow.

questions.stem: After a high test score, Sue says she is clever; after a low score, she says the test was unfair. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Correct. The self-serving bias is the tendency to credit our successes to ourselves and blame our failures on outside factors.
A pessimistic explanatory style is the habit of explaining bad events as lasting, affecting everything and caused by oneself.
The fundamental attribution error is the tendency, when judging other people's behavior, to overestimate personal traits and underestimate the situation.
Relative deprivation is the feeling of being worse off than the people one compares oneself with.

questions.explanation: The self-serving bias is the tendency to credit our successes to ourselves and blame our failures on outside factors.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes infantile amnesia?

options.text: The loss of memories from before an injury or illness
options.why: That describes retrograde amnesia.

options.text: The inability to form new memories after an injury or illness
options.why: That describes anterograde amnesia.

options.text: A progressive brain disease that destroys memory and then other mental abilities
options.why: That describes Alzheimer's disease.

options.text: The inability of adults to remember events from the first few years of life
options.why: Correct. This is what infantile amnesia means.

questions.explanation: Infantile amnesia is the inability of adults to remember events from the first few years of life.

questions.stem: Fourteen-year-old Jo refuses to go to school because she is sure everyone will stare at the small spot on her chin. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Pretend play is the play in which children act out imaginary roles and situations.
The personal fable is the belief of adolescents that they are unique and that bad things will not happen to them.
Parallel play is the play of young children who play side by side without interacting.
Correct. The imaginary audience is the belief of adolescents that everyone is watching and judging them.

questions.explanation: The imaginary audience is the belief of adolescents that everyone is watching and judging them.

questions.stem: Another research team repeats this study with new subjects and obtains the same result. What is this called?

options.why: Correct. Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.
That is explaining the study to participants afterward.
That is how subjects are placed in conditions.
That is an in-depth study of one individual.

questions.explanation: Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.

questions.stem: The smell of sunscreen instantly brings back a vivid memory of a childhood holiday. Which sense has this close link to emotion and memory areas?

options.why: Gustation is the sense of taste, which detects sweet, sour, salty, bitter, umami and oleogustus.
A pheromone is a chemical signal released by one member of a species that affects the behavior of others.
Correct. Olfaction is the sense of smell, the only sense that does not pass through the thalamus first.
A supertaster is a person with more taste receptors than average, who experiences tastes more intensely.

questions.explanation: Olfaction is the sense of smell, the only sense that does not pass through the thalamus first.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes altruism?

options.text: The expectation that people will help those who need help, even at a cost to themselves
options.why: That describes the social responsibility norm.

options.text: A psychologist who studies behavior in the workplace to improve productivity and well-being
options.why: That describes an industrial-organizational psychologist.

options.text: The expectation that people will help those who have helped them
options.why: That describes the social reciprocity norm.

options.text: Unselfish concern for the welfare of others
options.why: Correct. This is what altruism means.

questions.explanation: Altruism is unselfish concern for the welfare of others.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the method of loci?

options.text: A memory aid that uses vivid images or organizing tricks
options.why: That describes a mnemonic device.

options.text: The mnemonic of imagining items placed at locations along a familiar route
options.why: Correct. This is what the method of loci means.

options.text: The organizing of items into familiar, manageable units
options.why: That describes chunking.

options.text: Study that is crammed into one long session
options.why: That describes massed practice.

questions.explanation: The method of loci is the mnemonic of imagining items placed at locations along a familiar route.

questions.stem: A drug produces a rush of pleasure by flooding the brain's reward pathway. Which neurotransmitter is most directly involved?

options.why: Endorphins is the neurotransmitters that reduce pain and increase pleasure.
Glutamate is the brain's main excitatory neurotransmitter, which is involved in memory.
GABA is the brain's main inhibitory neurotransmitter.
Correct. Dopamine is the neurotransmitter that influences movement, attention, and feelings of reward.

questions.explanation: Dopamine is the neurotransmitter that influences movement, attention, and feelings of reward.

questions.stem: Which statement describes the directionality problem in this study?

options.text: It is unclear whether the first measure influences the second or the second influences the first
options.why: Correct. A correlation cannot show which variable, if either, comes first.

options.text: It is unclear whether the correlation is positive or negative
options.why: The sign of r shows the direction of the relationship.

options.text: It is unclear whether the two measures were recorded
options.why: Both measures were recorded.

options.text: It is unclear how many people took part
options.why: The sample size is stated.

questions.explanation: A correlation cannot show which variable, if either, comes first.

questions.stem: Which of the following would be a confounding variable in this study?

options.text: The two groups differed in the reporting of an emergency at the end of the study
options.why: That is the dependent variable, the result being measured.

options.text: The rooms used for the groups of five were much noisier
options.why: Correct. It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

options.text: Each one was assigned to a condition at random
options.why: Random assignment reduces confounding; it is not a confound.

options.text: One group differed from the other in the number of other people present
options.why: That is the independent variable itself.

questions.explanation: It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the theory that people are motivated to keep an ideal level of alertness and stimulation?

options.why: Homeostasis is the body's tendency to keep its internal state, such as temperature, steady.
Correct. Arousal theory is the theory that people are motivated to keep an ideal level of alertness and stimulation.
Incentive theory is the theory that behavior is pulled by rewards from outside the person.
Drive-reduction theory is the theory that a physical need creates a state of tension that motivates behavior to reduce it.

questions.explanation: Arousal theory is the theory that people are motivated to keep an ideal level of alertness and stimulation.

questions.stem: Why did the researchers assign the children to the two conditions at random?

options.text: So that the two groups would be similar at the start, and any difference could be attributed to the independent variable
options.why: Correct. Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

options.text: So that nobody would know the hypothesis
options.why: That describes a blind procedure.

options.text: So that the study would have more participants
options.why: Random assignment does not change the sample size.

options.text: So that the results could be generalized to the whole population
options.why: That is the purpose of random sampling, not random assignment.

questions.explanation: Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the pattern of negative thoughts about oneself, the world and the future that is found in depression?

options.why: Cognitive restructuring is the technique of identifying irrational thoughts and replacing them with more realistic ones.
Correct. The cognitive triad is the pattern of negative thoughts about oneself, the world and the future that is found in depression.
Rational emotive behavior therapy is the confrontational cognitive therapy, developed by Ellis, that actively challenges a client's irrational beliefs.
Cognitive-behavioral therapy is the therapy that combines changing self-defeating thoughts with changing behavior.

questions.explanation: The cognitive triad is the pattern of negative thoughts about oneself, the world and the future that is found in depression.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results is best supported?

options.text: The independent variable had a large effect
options.why: The averages are close and the difference is not significant.

options.text: The study shows that the two conditions always give identical results
options.why: A non-significant result does not show that there is no effect at all.

options.text: The difference between the groups is statistically significant
options.why: A p value of 0.41 is far above 0.05.

options.text: The difference between the groups is not statistically significant, so it could easily be due to chance
options.why: Correct. A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

questions.explanation: A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

questions.stem: What does the correlation show?

options.text: Higher values of the first measure tend to go with lower values of the second
options.why: That would be a negative correlation.

options.text: The first measure causes the second
options.why: A correlation does not show cause and effect.

options.text: Higher values of the first measure tend to go with higher values of the second
options.why: Correct. A positive correlation means the two measures tend to move in the same direction.
A correlation of zero would show no relationship.

questions.explanation: A positive correlation means the two measures tend to move in the same direction.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as in humanistic theory, the inborn drive of people to grow and fulfill their potential?

options.why: Unconditional positive regard is the attitude of total acceptance toward another person, whatever they say or do.
A defense mechanism is in psychodynamic theory, a method the ego uses without awareness to reduce anxiety by distorting reality.
Correct. The self-actualizing tendency is in humanistic theory, the inborn drive of people to grow and fulfill their potential.
The unconscious is in psychodynamic theory, the store of thoughts, wishes and memories that a person is not aware of but that still influences behavior.

questions.explanation: The self-actualizing tendency is in humanistic theory, the inborn drive of people to grow and fulfill their potential.

questions.stem: Asked about his future, Cole shrugs; he has not thought about it and does not care to. Which identity status is this?

options.why: Identity achievement is the identity status of a person who has explored options and made a commitment.
Identity foreclosure is the identity status of a person who has made a commitment without exploring options.
Identity moratorium is the identity status of a person who is actively exploring options but has not yet made a commitment.
Correct. Identity diffusion is the identity status of a person who has neither explored options nor made a commitment.

questions.explanation: Identity diffusion is the identity status of a person who has neither explored options nor made a commitment.

questions.stem: Divers who learned a word list underwater recall it better underwater than on land. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: A retrieval cue is a stimulus that helps bring a memory to mind.
The testing effect is the finding that practicing retrieval improves memory more than rereading.
Correct. Context-dependent memory is the improved recall that occurs in the same place where the information was learned.
Metacognition is the awareness and understanding of one's own thinking and learning.

questions.explanation: Context-dependent memory is the improved recall that occurs in the same place where the information was learned.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes assimilation?

options.text: A mental grouping of similar objects, events, ideas or people
options.why: That describes a concept.

options.text: The changing of an existing schema to fit new information
options.why: That describes accommodation.

options.text: The best or most typical example of a category
options.why: That describes a prototype.

options.text: The interpretation of a new experience in terms of an existing schema
options.why: Correct. This is what assimilation means.

questions.explanation: Assimilation is the interpretation of a new experience in terms of an existing schema.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the tendency to approach a problem in a way that has worked before, even when it no longer works?

options.why: Executive functions is the mental processes used to plan, organize and carry out goal-directed behavior.
Correct. A mental set is the tendency to approach a problem in a way that has worked before, even when it no longer works.
Divergent thinking is thinking that produces many possible answers to a problem.
Functional fixedness is the inability to see that an object can be used for something other than its usual purpose.

questions.explanation: A mental set is the tendency to approach a problem in a way that has worked before, even when it no longer works.

questions.stem: Neither the participants nor the assistants who recorded the results knew which condition each participant was in. What is this procedure called?

options.why: Correct. Keeping both participants and researchers unaware of the conditions reduces bias from expectations.
Random sampling is how participants are chosen from a population.
That is a therapy technique, not a research control.
In a single-blind procedure only the participants are unaware.

questions.explanation: Keeping both participants and researchers unaware of the conditions reduces bias from expectations.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes subjective well-being?

options.text: The positive character traits, such as kindness or curiosity, that are most central to a particular person
options.why: That describes signature strengths.

options.text: The ability to recover and adapt well after stress or hardship
options.why: That describes resilience.

options.text: A person's own evaluation of how happy and satisfied they are with life
options.why: Correct. This is what subjective well-being means.

options.text: The scientific study of the strengths and conditions that help people and communities thrive
options.why: That describes positive psychology.

questions.explanation: Subjective well-being is a person's own evaluation of how happy and satisfied they are with life.

questions.stem: A second study of a different pair of measures finds r = −0.68. Which relationship is stronger?

options.text: The relationship with the positive sign, whatever its size
options.why: The sign shows direction, not strength.

options.text: Neither, because relationships with different signs cannot be compared
options.why: Strength can be compared by distance from zero.

options.text: The relationship in the second study, because its coefficient is farther from zero
options.why: Correct. The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

options.text: The relationship in the first study, because its coefficient is closer to zero
options.why: A coefficient closer to zero shows a weaker relationship.

questions.explanation: The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

questions.stem: Kim remembers exactly where she sat and what she ate at her tenth birthday party. Which kind of memory is this?

options.why: Semantic memory is the explicit memory of facts and general knowledge.
Correct. Episodic memory is the explicit memory of personally experienced events.
Prospective memory is the memory to carry out a planned action in the future.
Procedural memory is the implicit memory of how to perform skills and actions.

questions.explanation: Episodic memory is the explicit memory of personally experienced events.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a delusion?

options.text: A false belief, often of persecution or grandeur, that a person holds despite clear evidence against it
options.why: Correct. This is what a delusion means.

options.text: The jumbled, illogical speech, sometimes called word salad, that is a symptom of schizophrenia
options.why: That describes disorganized speech.

options.text: A disturbance of movement in which a person may remain motionless for hours or move without purpose
options.why: That describes catatonia.

options.text: A lack of emotional expression in the face and voice
options.why: That describes flat affect.

questions.explanation: A delusion is a false belief, often of persecution or grandeur, that a person holds despite clear evidence against it.

questions.stem: In a crowd of fans, people see the red-shirted fans as one group and the blue-shirted fans as another. Which Gestalt principle explains this?

options.why: Proximity is the Gestalt principle that we group together objects that are near each other.
Correct. Similarity is the Gestalt principle that we group together objects that look alike.
Figure and ground is the Gestalt principle that we organize a scene into an object that stands out and its background.
Closure is the Gestalt principle that we fill in gaps to see a complete, whole object.

questions.explanation: Similarity is the Gestalt principle that we group together objects that look alike.

questions.stem: Dana must choose between two universities, both of which she would love to attend. Which kind of conflict is this?

options.why: Intrinsic motivation is the desire to do something for its own sake, because it is enjoyable or satisfying.
An avoidance-avoidance conflict is a conflict in which a person must choose between two unattractive options.
An approach-avoidance conflict is a conflict in which one option has both attractive and unattractive features.
Correct. An approach-approach conflict is a conflict in which a person must choose between two attractive options.

questions.explanation: An approach-approach conflict is a conflict in which a person must choose between two attractive options.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes blindsight?

options.text: The ability to respond to visual information without consciously seeing it
options.why: Correct. This is what blindsight means.

options.text: The theory that color is processed in opposing pairs: red–green, blue–yellow and black–white
options.why: That describes the opponent-process theory.

options.text: The theory that the retina has three types of color receptors, sensitive to red, green and blue
options.why: That describes the trichromatic theory.

options.text: The inability to recognize faces, even familiar ones, after brain damage
options.why: That describes prosopagnosia.

questions.explanation: Blindsight is the ability to respond to visual information without consciously seeing it.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes avoidant personality disorder?

options.text: The personality disorder marked by lasting distrust and suspicion of others
options.why: That describes paranoid personality disorder.

options.text: The personality disorder marked by excessive emotion and attention seeking
options.why: That describes histrionic personality disorder.

options.text: The personality disorder marked by extreme sensitivity to rejection and avoidance of social contact
options.why: Correct. This is what avoidant personality disorder means.

options.text: The personality disorder marked by unstable moods, relationships and self-image, and by impulsive behavior
options.why: That describes borderline personality disorder.

questions.explanation: Avoidant personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by extreme sensitivity to rejection and avoidance of social contact.

questions.stem: Why did the researchers assign the children to the two conditions at random?

options.text: So that the two groups would be similar at the start, and any difference could be attributed to the independent variable
options.why: Correct. Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

options.text: So that the study would have more participants
options.why: Random assignment does not change the sample size.

options.text: So that nobody would know the hypothesis
options.why: That describes a blind procedure.

options.text: So that the results could be generalized to the whole population
options.why: That is the purpose of random sampling, not random assignment.

questions.explanation: Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

questions.stem: In which structure of the inner ear do hair cells convert sound vibrations into neural signals?

options.why: Wavelength is the distance from one wave peak to the next, which determines the hue of light.
Amplitude is the height of a sound wave, which determines loudness.
Frequency is the number of sound waves per second, which determines pitch.
Correct. The cochlea is the coiled, fluid-filled tube in the inner ear where sound waves become neural impulses.

questions.explanation: The cochlea is the coiled, fluid-filled tube in the inner ear where sound waves become neural impulses.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a hallucinogen?

options.text: A drug, such as heroin, that relieves pain by acting on endorphin receptors and is highly addictive
options.why: That describes an opioid.

options.text: A drug, such as alcohol, that slows neural activity and body functions
options.why: That describes a depressant.

options.text: A drug, such as marijuana, that distorts perception and can cause sensory experiences without sensory input
options.why: Correct. This is what a hallucinogen means.

options.text: A drug, such as caffeine or cocaine, that speeds up neural activity and body functions
options.why: That describes a stimulant.

questions.explanation: A hallucinogen is a drug, such as marijuana, that distorts perception and can cause sensory experiences without sensory input.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the fovea?

options.text: The point where the optic nerve leaves the eye, which has no receptor cells
options.why: That describes the blind spot.

options.text: The receptor cells that detect color and fine detail and work in bright light
options.why: That describes cones.

options.text: The central point of the retina, where cones are packed most densely and vision is sharpest
options.why: Correct. This is what the fovea means.

options.text: The light-sensitive inner surface at the back of the eye that contains the receptor cells
options.why: That describes the retina.

questions.explanation: The fovea is the central point of the retina, where cones are packed most densely and vision is sharpest.

questions.stem: After being rejected by a university, Hal says, 'I never really wanted to go there anyway; it is too far away.' Which defense mechanism is this?

options.why: Correct. Rationalization is the defense mechanism of giving a comfortable excuse in place of the real reason for a behavior.
Projection is the defense mechanism of seeing one's own unacceptable impulses in other people.
Denial is the defense mechanism of refusing to accept a painful reality.
Displacement is the defense mechanism of shifting an impulse from its real target to a safer one.

questions.explanation: Rationalization is the defense mechanism of giving a comfortable excuse in place of the real reason for a behavior.

questions.stem: Ed feels strong resentment toward his sister but treats her with exaggerated kindness and praise. Which defense mechanism is this?

options.why: Repression is the defense mechanism of pushing anxiety-arousing thoughts and memories out of awareness.
Regression is the defense mechanism of retreating to behavior from an earlier stage of development.
Correct. Reaction formation is the defense mechanism of acting in the opposite way to one's unacceptable impulses.
Sublimation is the defense mechanism of turning unacceptable impulses into socially valued activities.

questions.explanation: Reaction formation is the defense mechanism of acting in the opposite way to one's unacceptable impulses.

questions.stem: Which statement describes the directionality problem in this study?

options.text: It is unclear whether the two measures were recorded
options.why: Both measures were recorded.

options.text: It is unclear how many people took part
options.why: The sample size is stated.

options.text: It is unclear whether the first measure influences the second or the second influences the first
options.why: Correct. A correlation cannot show which variable, if either, comes first.

options.text: It is unclear whether the correlation is positive or negative
options.why: The sign of r shows the direction of the relationship.

questions.explanation: A correlation cannot show which variable, if either, comes first.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes problem-focused coping?

options.text: The weakening of the body's defenses against illness during long-term stress
options.why: That describes immune suppression.

options.text: The reducing of stress by changing the stressor itself or the way one deals with it
options.why: Correct. This is what problem-focused coping means.

options.text: The reducing of stress by managing one's emotional reaction rather than the stressor
options.why: That describes emotion-focused coping.

options.text: Persistently high blood pressure, which is made more likely by chronic stress
options.why: That describes hypertension.

questions.explanation: Problem-focused coping is the reducing of stress by changing the stressor itself or the way one deals with it.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the axon?

options.text: The tiny gap between the sending neuron and the receiving neuron
options.why: That describes the synapse.

options.text: The part of the neuron that contains the nucleus and keeps the cell alive
options.why: That describes the cell body.

options.text: The long fiber that carries the neural impulse away from the cell body toward other cells
options.why: Correct. This is what the axon means.

options.text: The fatty layer around some axons that speeds up neural impulses
options.why: That describes the myelin sheath.

questions.explanation: The axon is the long fiber that carries the neural impulse away from the cell body toward other cells.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results is best supported?

options.text: The two groups had the same average result
options.why: The table shows different averages.

options.text: The difference between the groups is statistically significant, so it is unlikely to be due to chance
options.why: Correct. A p value below 0.05 means a difference this large would rarely occur by chance alone.

options.text: The difference between the groups is probably due to chance
options.why: A p value of 0.01 is below 0.05, so chance is an unlikely explanation.

options.text: The results prove that every individual in the first group differed from every individual in the second
options.why: The table reports group averages, not individual scores.

questions.explanation: A p value below 0.05 means a difference this large would rarely occur by chance alone.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the refractory period?

options.text: The rule that a neuron either fires at full strength or does not fire at all
options.why: That describes the all-or-nothing principle.

options.text: The brief pause after a neuron fires during which it cannot fire again
options.why: Correct. This is what the refractory period means.

options.text: The change in which positive ions rush into the axon and make the inside less negative
options.why: That describes depolarization.

options.text: The level of stimulation that must be reached for a neuron to fire
options.why: That describes the threshold.

questions.explanation: The refractory period is the brief pause after a neuron fires during which it cannot fire again.

questions.stem: Scores on a test are normally distributed with a mean of 70 and a standard deviation of 15. About what percentage of scores are between 40 and 100?

options.why: This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.
This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.
This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.
Correct. About 95% of scores fall within two standard deviations of the mean.

questions.explanation: About 95% of scores fall within two standard deviations of the mean. (55 and 85 are one standard deviation from the mean; 40 and 100 are two.)

questions.stem: At age four, Noah learns to hold a pencil correctly and to fasten buttons. These are examples of which of the following?

options.why: A teratogen is a harmful agent, such as alcohol or a virus, that can damage an embryo or fetus.
Gross motor skills is the movements that use large muscles, such as crawling, walking and jumping.
Correct. Fine motor skills is the movements that use small muscles, such as grasping a crayon or buttoning a shirt.
Imprinting is the process by which some animals form a strong attachment to the first moving object they see.

questions.explanation: Fine motor skills is the movements that use small muscles, such as grasping a crayon or buttoning a shirt.

questions.stem: A fifteen-year-old debates what would happen to society if people could live forever. Which of Piaget's stages allows this hypothetical thinking?

options.why: The sensorimotor stage is Piaget's stage from birth to about age 2, in which infants know the world through senses and actions.
The concrete operational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 7 to 11, in which children think logically about real objects and events.
The preoperational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 2 to 7, in which children use words and images but cannot yet reason logically.
Correct. The formal operational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 12 on, in which people can reason about abstract and hypothetical ideas.

questions.explanation: The formal operational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 12 on, in which people can reason about abstract and hypothetical ideas.

questions.stem: People who take a personality test in March get almost the same scores when they take it again in May. Which quality does the test have?

options.why: Standardization is the giving and scoring of a test in the same way for everyone, and the comparison of scores with a pretested group.
Construct validity is the extent to which a test measures the concept it claims to measure.
Correct. Test-retest reliability is the consistency of scores when the same people take the same test twice.
Split-half reliability is the consistency of scores between two halves of the same test.

questions.explanation: Test-retest reliability is the consistency of scores when the same people take the same test twice.

questions.stem: A father first guides his daughter's hands as she ties her shoes, then only gives hints, then lets her do it alone. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: The zone of proximal development is the gap between what a learner can do alone and what the learner can do with help.
Dementia is a serious decline in memory and thinking that interferes with daily life, most common in old age.
Fluid intelligence is the ability to reason quickly and abstractly, which tends to decline in older adulthood.
Correct. Scaffolding is the temporary support that a more skilled person gives a learner and gradually removes.

questions.explanation: Scaffolding is the temporary support that a more skilled person gives a learner and gradually removes.

questions.stem: A survey's sample has the same proportions of ages, incomes and regions as the whole country. Which term describes this sample?

options.why: A convenience sample is a sample made up of whoever is easiest for the researcher to reach.
Random assignment is the placing of participants in experimental conditions by chance.
Correct. A representative sample is a sample whose characteristics match those of the population it is drawn from.
Sampling bias is a flaw in selecting participants that makes the sample unlike the population.

questions.explanation: A representative sample is a sample whose characteristics match those of the population it is drawn from.

questions.title: Article analysis: a study of attention to the road

parts.prompt: Identify the research method used in the study.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the method as an experiment.
rubric.example: The study is an experiment: the researchers manipulated a variable and randomly assigned the subjects to conditions.

parts.prompt: State the operational definition of attention to the road.

rubric.criterion: States how the variable was measured in this study.
rubric.example: Attention to the road was defined as the number of road signs out of 30 that each participant failed to notice.

parts.prompt: Describe the meaning of the difference between the two group averages.

rubric.criterion: Accurately describes which group scored higher or lower and what that means for the variable measured.
rubric.example: The phone group missed more road signs. On average, the value was 11.4 for the group that talked on the phone and 4.9 for the group that drove without a phone, and a p value of 0.01 means a difference this large is unlikely to be due to chance.

parts.prompt: Identify at least one ethical guideline applied by the researchers.

rubric.criterion: Identifies an ethical guideline that the summary shows was followed.
rubric.example: Informed consent: participants agreed to take part after being told about the study. (Also acceptable: debriefing; the right to withdraw; approval by an institutional review board.)

parts.prompt: Explain the extent to which the research findings may or may not be generalizable, using specific and relevant evidence from the study.

rubric.criterion: Explains a limit (or strength) of generalizability with reference to the sample.
rubric.example: The sample was 64 licensed drivers from one city, so the findings may not apply to people of other ages, cultures or backgrounds. Because the sample was not randomly selected from a wider population, it may not be representative.

parts.prompt: Explain how at least one of the research findings supports or refutes the researchers' hypothesis.

rubric.criterion: Uses a specific finding from the study as evidence.
rubric.example: The phone group missed more road signs. (11.4 compared with 4.9).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the finding supports the hypothesis, using a psychological concept.
rubric.example: This supports the hypothesis that phone use affects attention to the road. Because subjects were randomly assigned, the difference can be attributed to phone use. The finding illustrates selective attention and inattentional blindness: attention is limited, so people fail to notice visible objects when attention is elsewhere.

questions.title: Evidence-based question: Which study methods lead to the best long-term learning?

parts.prompt: Propose a specific and defensible claim, based in psychological science, that responds to the question.

rubric.criterion: States a claim that answers the question and can be supported by the sources.
rubric.example: Spacing study sessions and testing oneself lead to better long-term learning than cramming or rereading.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using at least one piece of specific and relevant evidence from one of the sources. (ii) Explain how the evidence supports your claim, using a psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding learned in AP Psychology.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from one source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source A, students who spread their study over six days recalled 27 of 40 words a month later, compared with 16 for students who studied in one session.

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through the spacing effect: distributed practice gives repeated chances to encode and consolidate the material, so it is retained longer than with massed practice.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a psychological concept in the explanation.
rubric.example: The concept must be named and applied correctly, as in the model explanation.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using an additional piece of specific and relevant evidence from a different source. (ii) Explain how this evidence supports your claim, using a different psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from a different source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source B, students who took practice quizzes scored 68 percent a week later, compared with 49 percent for students who reread the passage.

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through the testing effect: retrieving information from memory strengthens the memory and its retrieval cues more than rereading does.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a different psychological concept from the one used in part B.
rubric.example: The concept must differ from the one used in part B and be applied correctly.
